summary: Careful, well-documented preregistered paired evaluation of a verifier-in-the-loop (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration using gpt-5-mini. Execution and artifact records are complete and reproducible. Confirmatory result is a degenerate null (both baseline and guarded arms passed forbidden-reachability on all N=300 pairs). Manuscript is scientifically responsible but requires specific clarifications to ensure correct interpretation of the null result and to document certain design choices that materially affect inference.
critical_issues: The primary estimand comparison is degenerate because every paired outcome is identical (n11=300, n10=n01=0). The manuscript must more explicitly acknowledge that with zero discordant pairs the confirmatory test provides no evidence that GVR would reduce forbidden-reachability in settings where baseline generation produces any violations; the current framing risks overinterpreting a null as evidence of 'no effect' rather than an outcome of task/design selection.

The experimental design used shared_initial_generation (single shared LLM candidate per intent pair) and recorded zero applied repairs across all guarded episodes. The manuscript does not currently report the total number of repair attempts, the criteria/triggers for invoking a repair attempt, or why no repairs were applied; this omission impedes interpretation of whether the GVR pipeline was actually exercised.

The shared-initial-generation semantics and the observed zero repair-application rate materially constrain what the paired comparison can test. The paper must explicitly explain and justify (using the preregistration and execution logs/artifacts) this design choice and discuss its implications for the primary estimand, model-call overhead, and inferential power.

Validator configuration and provenance are insufficiently detailed in the main text: the paper names Batfish and a lightweight static analyzer but must report exact validator identifiers/versions, key configuration settings used to define forbidden reachability, and stable artifact references/hashes to the validator configuration files (all available in the evidence bundle). Without these details the reproducibility and scope of the safety predicate are under-specified.

The contamination/fingerprint and deduplication checks are only cursorily described in text. The manuscript must state the contamination_summary results (explicitly report that no contamination flags were raised and provide the path/hash to contamination_summary.csv) and discuss the remaining potential for training-data overlap as prespecified in the preregistration.
required_revisions: Add explicit counts and provenance for repair activity: report the number of guard-condition repair attempts invoked, number actually issued to the model, and number of repairs applied (use execution/provider_calls and validator_trace artifacts). If repair_prompt_sha256 is null and repair_applied=false throughout, state that fact and explain why the verifier never requested a repair (include the deterministic decision logic and the relevant artifact paths/hashes).

Add a short, explicit subsection (or paragraphs) explaining the shared_initial_generation design (generation_semantics value), why independent-condition generation was not used, and how this choice affects the interpretation of the primary estimand and model-call overhead. Cite the preregistration fields and the execution manifest (model_calls_used=300, maximum_model_calls=600).

Revise the Results and Discussion to explicitly treat the confirmatory null as a degenerate outcome due to no observed discordance; include text stating that McNemar-style inference is uninformative in this case and that the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline violation rate. Describe how this limits conclusions about GVR efficacy in more challenging settings and avoid wording that could be read as general evidence that verifiers are unnecessary.

Insert explicit validator provenance and configuration details into Methods or Disclosure: Batfish container image name and version, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 identifier and version, static analyzer version and key parameters, and artifact path(s)/hash(es) for validator configuration files (these exist in the archived evidence bundle).

Explicitly report the contamination summary result (analysis/contamination_summary.csv): state that no flags were raised (or summarize flagged counts if any) and reference the artifact path and hash from the manifest. Also state how flagged items would have been handled per the preregistration and reference the deterministic deduplication rule outputs in the execution artifacts.
optional_revisions: Briefly illustrate (one or two short examples) a representative adversarial intent that the task generator produced and show the corresponding shared initial candidate and validator trace (use the provided representative task artifacts). This can clarify dataset difficulty without adding new experiments.

Expand the Threats to Validity section to more explicitly connect the degenerate result to recommendations for constructing stronger adversarial intent generation and for alternative experimental contracts (independent-condition generation or increased repair budget) that would better stress-test GVR.

If space permits, include a brief table listing the most relevant artifact file paths and their representative hashes (execution/manifests and key analysis CSVs) to help readers locate reproducibility evidence in the bundle.
